title: Prefill probe decisioning and rollback orchestration
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Background: We need a runtime component that makes per-request decisions about whether to route a request to an optimistic (fast, lower-cost) decoder path using a prefill probe, or to the conservative path. This ticket designs and implements the decisioning and rollback orchestration layer: a state machine that interprets probe signals, computes an acceptance score, triggers graceful rollbacks when acceptance falls below thresholds, and exposes observability and controls for SRE/PM to tune behavior. Goals: 1) Define acceptance metrics (confidence, latency delta, token bias) and a compact score used by the router. 2) Design the rollback orchestration so the runtime can abort optimistic output and seamlessly continue on the fallback model without client-visible corruption. 3) Implement safe rollout controls (canary percentage, decay timers, circuit breaker) and runtime knobs for batch/latency trade-offs. 4) Add telemetry and dashboards for per-model acceptance curves and rollback frequency. Non-goals: model selection heuristics for training (handled by model-onboarding). This ticket focuses on runtime orchestration and metrics integration.
acceptance_criteria: Router computes a normalized acceptance score per request and persists it to trace/span
If acceptance < configured threshold, runtime triggers rollback and replays remaining tokens on fallback model without duplicate tokens or user-visible gaps
Rollback latency contribution measured and documented; median rollback penalty < 50ms for 90% of rollbacks on p99-prefill sizes
Control plane exposes canary percentage, per-model threshold, and circuit-breaker status via Console
Grafana dashboard shows acceptance histogram, rollback rate, and model-level latency deltas over time
E2E test harness simulates probe false accepts and false rejects and validates content continuity post-rollback
notes: Design trade-offs: We considered two rollback strategies: (A) prefetch-and-stitch where the optimistic path generates tokens to completion and we stitch fallback continuation when necessary; (B) progressive-swap where the fallback takes over mid-sequence and we avoid stitching by maintaining shared token index. Chosen: progressive-swap (B) due to lower memory and simpler KV cache semantics across GPUs.

Kernel/attention concern: progressive-swap requires a KV cache replay for the fallback model starting from the last confirmed token. To minimize replay cost we will leverage prefix KV reuse and checksum-hashed cache compatibility checks between model variants.

Safety: For sensitive workloads (private deployments) default acceptance threshold is conservative and circuit breaker is stricter. PM requested an additional label to mark endpoints with high hallucination risk.
Operational runbook draft added to Confluence. Includes steps for manual rollback of router weights, and instructions to temporarily disable speculative probes per-model via Console toggle.
